headline: Easy Fox, a four-person game studio, says it took out a bank loan to pay the AI running costs of the free demo of its driving-lesson game, which Kotaku says come to more than $1,000 a day.
score_reason: Pool 2 kept: a light story about one small studio's costs, confirmed only by its own Steam update as relayed by Kotaku.
importance_line: Small game studios, and eventually players through the game's price, bear the cost of live AI chat when a demo suddenly becomes popular, but the figures come from the studio's own update as relayed by Kotaku and the studio has not decided to close the demo.
summary: Kotaku reports that Easy Fox, the four-person studio behind the upcoming game Teach My Little Sister How To Drive, says in a Steam update that its demo players grew more than twentyfold in a month and that the cost of the AI chatbot playing the learner driver forced it to take out a bank loan. The studio switched from Google's Gemini to an OpenAI model after usage-limit errors, says it will have to factor the costs into the game's price, and warns it may have to close the demo early but has not decided to.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched Kotaku text. The $1,000 a day is Kotaku's 'apparently' figure. Steam update not opened.
